newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling opens week stable, still rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling opens week stable, still rangebound.

text.p: The shilling opened the week stable on Monday in brisk trading, but remained rangebound, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.93 unchanged against the dollar while against the pound was posted at a mean rate of 87.88 from 87.55 on Friday.
This is the fourth week the shilling has traded within the narrow band of 54.85/55.00. Dealers attributed this to several interventions by the Central Bank to stem the shilling's rise.
"I don't know what's going to jumpstart the shilling from its current position, a dealer said. "You see the flows are balanced and nobody's speculating," he added.
Another dealer said there was little incentive to trade.
They said in the absence of any significant changes ahead, the shilling was likely to remain stable in the short-term.
On Friday, Central Bank Governor Micah Cheserem hinted at shilling losses in the coming days.
"We are conscious of the fact that the recent trends in the shilling exchange rate may be hurting exporters," Cheserem told a meeting of horticulture exporters.

"We at the central bank would therefore have no objection to a progressive movement in the shilling exchange rate to levels acceptable to both importers and exporters as long as the movement is in response to economic fundamentals," he added.
Cheserem emphasised that any action taken by the central bank to align the shilling exchange rate or ease the high level of interest rates should not generate inflationary pressures.
On Monday, the money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at 10 percent compared to below 10 percent on Friday.
The market was expected to tighten later during the week on tax payments.
